subject: science

Convection currents in the mantle make the plates move very slowly, a few centimetres each year. At the boundaries the plates push, pull or slide past each other, but they often get stuck, so stress builds up in the rocks. When the rocks suddenly break, the energy is released as seismic waves and the ground shakes. That is why countries on plate boundaries, like Japan and Turkey, have many earthquakes, but Egypt, which is mostly far from a boundary, has fewer.

The upthrust is equal to the weight of the water that the object pushes away (displaces). A ship is hollow and wide, so it displaces a very large amount of water and gets a big upthrust. Also, because it is full of air, the average density of the ship is less than the density of water. The nail is solid steel, so it is denser than water, and its weight is bigger than the small upthrust, so it sinks.

Simple stone lines across slopes also slow rainwater so that it soaks into the soil.

answer: Desertification is when the desert get bigger. It is because of global warming and factories. We must plant trees.

subject: science
stem: Explain how the human body keeps its temperature stable when the weather is very hot. In your answer, describe at least two ways the body loses heat and explain why sweating is important.
answer: The human body needs to stay at about 37 degrees Celsius, and when the weather is very hot the body uses different ways to lose heat. The first way is sweating. When we are hot, the sweat glands in our skin produce sweat, and when this water evaporates from the skin it takes heat with it. This cools the blood near the surface of the skin. The second way is vasodilation. The blood vessels near the skin become wider, so more warm blood flows close to the surface and the heat can go out to the air. Also, the hair on our skin lies flat, which helps the air to pass over the skin. Sweating is very important because evaporation is the most effective way to lose heat, especially when the air is hotter than our body. Without sweating we could get heat stroke. However, in very humid weather sweating works less well because the air is already full of water, so the sweat does not evaporate quickly. This is why we feel more uncomfortable in hot and humid days. The brain, especially the hypothalamus, controls all these changes automatically.

subject: humanities
stem: Discuss two important effects of the invention of the printing press in Europe in the fifteenth century. Explain why these effects were significant for society at that time.
answer:
The printing press, invented by Johannes Gutenberg around 1440, had many important effects on European society. In this essay I will discuss two of them: the spread of knowledge and the change in religion.

Firstly, the printing press made books much cheaper and faster to produce. Before this invention, books were copied by hand by monks, so they were very expensive and only rich people could own them. After the printing press, thousands of copies of a book could be made in a short time. This meant that more people could read and learn new ideas, and literacy began to grow. This was significant because knowledge was no longer controlled by a small group of people.

Secondly, the printing press helped the Reformation. Martin Luther's ideas against the Catholic Church spread very quickly through printed pamphlets and books. People could read the Bible in their own language instead of only in Latin, so they could understand religion by themselves. This was significant because it weakened the power of the Church and changed the religious map of Europe.

In conclusion, the printing press changed society because it spread knowledge and ideas quickly, and it helped to create a more educated and more independent Europe.

subject: language
stem: Some people believe that learning a second language should be compulsory for all school children from a very young age. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this opinion? Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own experience.
answer:
In recent years, the question of whether learning a second language should be mandatory for all school children from a young age has sparked considerable debate. While some argue that it is essential, others believe it may be unnecessary. In my opinion, I strongly agree that learning a second language from an early age is beneficial for several reasons.

Firstly, children have a greater capacity to absorb new languages. Studies have shown that young learners can acquire pronunciation and vocabulary more easily than adults. For example, my younger brother started learning English at the age of six and now he speaks it fluently, whereas I started at twelve and I still struggle with pronunciation. This demonstrates that early exposure is advantageous.

Secondly, learning a second language improves cognitive skills. It enhances memory, problem-solving abilities, and creativity. Moreover, it fosters cultural awareness and open-mindedness, which are crucial in our globalized world.

However, some people argue that making it compulsory could put too much pressure on young children. They believe that children should focus on their mother tongue and other basic subjects first. While this is a valid concern, I think that if the lessons are fun and engaging, children will not feel stressed. In fact, they often enjoy learning through games and songs.

In conclusion, although there are some drawbacks, I believe that the benefits of compulsory second language learning from a young age outweigh the disadvantages. It not only improves cognitive abilities but also prepares children for a globalized society. Therefore, I strongly support making it a mandatory part of the curriculum.

subject: science
stem: Explain how the water cycle works and why it is important for life on Earth.
answer: The water cycle is a continuous process where water moves around the Earth. First, the sun heats water in oceans, rivers, and lakes, causing evaporation. Water turns into water vapor and rises into the atmosphere. Then, as the vapor cools, it condenses into tiny droplets that form clouds, this is called condensation. When the clouds become heavy, the water falls back to Earth as precipitation, which can be rain, snow, or hail. Some of this water goes into rivers and lakes, and some soaks into the ground to become groundwater. Plants also release water vapor through transpiration. Finally, the water collects in bodies of water and the cycle starts again. The water cycle is very important for life because it provides fresh water for drinking, agriculture, and for animals. Without it, there will be no fresh water and all living things will die. Also, it helps to distribute heat around the planet, which affects the climate. In conclusion, the water cycle is a vital natural process that sustains life on Earth.

subject: humanities
stem: Discuss the main causes and effects of the Industrial Revolution.

First, the invention of new machines such as the steam engine allowed factories to produce goods faster. Second, there was a lot of coal and iron available in Britain, which were needed for industry. Also, the population was growing, so there was more demand for products. Another cause was the improvement in agriculture, which meant fewer people were needed to work on farms, so they moved to cities to find jobs in factories. Working conditions in factories were very bad, with long hours and low pay, and children were often employed. Cities became overcrowded and polluted because of the factories and the large number of workers. In conclusion, the Industrial Revolution had many causes and its effects changed society in both good and bad ways.

stem: Explain why plants need sunlight to grow. Include what happens during photosynthesis and what would happen to a plant without sunlight.
answer: Plants need sunlight to grow because they make their own food using sunlight. This process is called photosynthesis. The water turns into water vapour and goes up into the air. This is called evaporation. Plants also release water vapour through their leaves, which is called transpiration. stem: Explain how the human digestive system breaks down food and absorbs nutrients. Include the roles of at least three organs and describe what happens to undigested material.
answer: The human digestive system is a long tube where food is broken down into smaller pieces and then absorbed into the blood. The process starts in the mouth, where teeth chew food into small pieces and saliva contains enzymes that begin to break down starch. After swallowing, the food goes down the oesophagus to the stomach. The stomach produces acid and enzymes that break down proteins and kill bacteria. Then the food moves to the small intestine, where most digestion and absorption happen. The small intestine receives enzymes from the pancreas and bile from the liver, which helps to digest fats. The walls of the small intestine have villi, which are tiny finger-like structures that increase the surface area for absorbing nutrients into the bloodstream. After the small intestine, the remaining undigested material, mainly fibre and water, goes to the large intestine. Here, water is absorbed back into the body. Finally, the leftover waste is stored in the rectum and leaves the body through the anus as faeces. This whole process usually takes about 24 to 72 hours.
